_readme: cdAfterbody = fixture pressure CD - nose-only pressure CD + fixture base CD; cylindrical afterbodies contribute base CD only. Coefficients use kernel max-diameter area, then refAreaScale. R-100 Figure 13(a), added 2026-10-07: six informational points, no gate changes; friction excluded, ISA sea level acceptable. Equation (1) is not used.
Machine-readable validation anchors. Provenance, tolerances and caveats for each dataset are recorded in the project's research notes; every anchor cites its source report below.
Scored by validation/score.mjs. Each series: quantity is one of cd | cdAfterbody | cdDelta | cpPctL | cpOverL | cnaPerRad | cnaPerDeg.

cdDelta = this cell's fixture total CD minus the series' referenceFixture total CD at the same Mach, both swept with the same flags and conditions; it scores a measured configuration-minus-configuration increment. A point may carry its own tolerance as a third element [mach, value, tol], which then overrides the series tol/relTol.
cd series carry base: 'included' (compare kernel total CD) or 'excluded' (compare kernel total minus base CD) to match each dataset's accounting.
tol is absolute in the anchor's unit; relTol is relative (fraction of the anchor value); gate=false series are informational (reported, never counted).
gateMinMach/gateMaxMach restrict which points count toward the gate; outside points report as info.
refAreaScale converts kernel-referenced coefficients (max body diameter area) to the dataset's reference area (kernel value x scale).

Re matching: fixtures MAY carry a machAlt table (Mach -> altitude m) which the sweep uses to evaluate each point at tunnel-matched Reynolds number (ARCAS and rma53d02 carry the Mach-Alt tables from Rogers' own CDX1 files). Fixtures WITHOUT machAlt (basic-finner, hb2) still sweep at ISA sea level - expect a friction-CD bias there, worst subsonic.

Same report, same quantity and same accounting as the fins-on cd-transonic-tunnel series above: C_A,corr, the axial-force coefficient CORRECTED TO FREE-STREAM CONDITIONS AT THE MODEL BASE (=> base EXCLUDED), at alpha = 0 and roll angle 0, which at alpha = 0 is the drag coefficient. The report's own words (p.4): 'Axial-force data were not corrected to free-stream conditions at the model base, except for the summary data at a roll angle of 0 deg and an angle of attack of 0 deg' - figures 11 and 12 ARE that summary data (p.5).

SOURCE UPGRADED 2026-08-25: THE REPORT ITSELF, replacing a quoted single-point figure read. Until this revision the anchor was C. E. Rogers' read posted on TRF 197207 #9 (Short 0.225, Long 0.250), never independently confirmed. NASA TN D-4013 has now been retrieved from NTRS (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19670020050/downloads/19670020050.pdf, 64 pp., scanned) and its Figures 11 (short model) and 12 (long model) digitized directly off the report's own page images at their native 2368x3104 / 2352x3072 resolution - about 2.8x the linear resolution of the forum reproduction. Method, verification, every point and the scoring consequences: scorecard-finsoff-figs-2026-08-25.md.

DIGITIZATION METHOD, reproducible: (1) Mach axis by least squares over the 17 printed vertical gridlines M0.50..M1.30, fit residual 0.00015 (Fig 11) / 0.00010 (Fig 12) Mach; (2) DE-SKEW - Fig 11's scan is rotated ~0.56 deg, measured on its C_A,corr zero axis (a heavy line clean across the panel, no curve within 0.22 of it) which falls 11.3 px left to right with a 0.22 px linear-fit residual; every column is shifted before anything is measured, and without it the two ends of a curve are biased +/-0.004; (3) coefficient axis by least squares over the 17 printed C_A,corr gridlines 0.80..0.00, fit residual 0.00019 / 0.00024 in C_A (~0.3 px); (4) curves separated by a value envelope plus a printed-gridline mask applied ONLY where the grid is actually drawn - measured per column as the fraction of the 17 gridline rows carrying ink, which shows Fig 11 draws its coefficient grid over M<=0.65 only and Fig 12 over M>=1.10 only.

VERIFIED FOUR WAYS BEFORE USE. (a) The same pipeline run against a completely independent image - the forum reproduction of the same two figures, 834x1125, JPEG-blurred - agrees to rms 0.0010 and max 0.0032 over 14 Mach numbers on both configs. (b) At M0.60 there are now four reads of this curve: 0.2214 (this, report scan), 0.2216 (this, forum image), 0.222 (this project, 2026-08-03) and 0.225 (Rogers) for Short; 0.2491 / 0.2495 / 0.248 / 0.250 for Long. Total spread 0.0036 and 0.0020. (c) The same pipeline reading the x_cp panel of Fig 11 reproduces an earlier independent digitization of that same panel to ~1 %L at all ten Machs. (d) The digitized curves reproduce the report's own prose about their crossover - 'the long model has higher C_A,corr coefficients than the short model at Mach numbers from 0.60 to 0.975. At Mach numbers from 0.975 to 1.20, the short model has higher C_A,corr values' (pp.5-6) - the read crossover lands at M0.975 exactly.

TOLERANCE +/-0.008. TIGHTER than the +/-0.010 it replaces, and now derived from the REPORT'S OWN STATED ACCURACY instead of a curve-read band. Root-sum-square of: C_A +/-0.004 (report p.4 accuracy table); the base correction, C_p,b +/-0.01 (same table) x A_b/S = 0.4225 (Fig 1(b) dimensions the tail-cone base at 0.65 d) = +/-0.0042; digitization +/-0.004 (bounded by the 0.0036 max spread across the four independent reads above); Mach +/-0.003 (report) x the local curve slope, <= 0.0012 in the flat and plateau bands. RSS = 0.0072, rounded UP to 0.008. NEVER widen. One gated point - Short M1.00 - sits on a steep local gradient where the same budget would justify +/-0.011; it is deliberately left at +/-0.008, because tightening is always permitted and it changes no verdict there.

ONLY THE REPORT'S OWN TEST MACH NUMBERS ARE GATED. p.4: 'Both models were investigated at Mach numbers of 0.60, 0.80, 0.90, 1.00, and 1.20. The short model was also investigated at a Mach number of 0.95.' Everything between those is the draftsman's fairing through them, not a measurement - so it is carried in cd0-finsoff-fairing as gate:false, visible in every scorecard and never counted. That is why the short cell gates 6 points and the long cell 5.

CAVEAT ON THE GEOMETRY, PART 1: 'fins off' means the fins were taken off THIS model. The body keeps its 15-degree boat tail, so this is still not the plain-body (finless, NO-boat-tail) cell README lists as missing, and the fixture keeps the boat tail to match.

CAVEAT ON THE GEOMETRY, PART 2 - PREVIOUSLY OPEN, NOW RESOLVED FROM THE REPORT, AND IT IS ASYMMETRIC BETWEEN THE TWO CELLS. p.3: 'The fin anchors (fig. 1(b)) were used to plug the slots in the boattailed afterbody when the short model was investigated without fins, whereas the slots were plugged with balsa and faired flush with the model skin when the long model was investigated without fins.' So the SHORT fins-off article carries four un-faired fin anchors that no fixture models, and the LONG fins-off article is aerodynamically clean. The report attributes the short curve rising ABOVE the long one at M0.975-1.20 to exactly that (p.6: 'This trend is also attributed to the fin anchors, which were not flush with the model skin on the short model'). The bias is one-sided and in our disfavour - the short anchor value includes protuberance drag we do not model, so our short-model excess is UNDERSTATED. It is a known bias, not a measurement uncertainty, and the tolerance is NOT widened for it.

OTHER FACTS SETTLED BY HAVING THE REPORT. The models WERE boundary-layer tripped: 'In order to obtain turbulent flow over the model, a 0.25-cm-wide (0.10-in.) strip of No. 120 carborundum grains was affixed around the model 3.17 cm (1.25 in.) aft of the nose and 1.27 cm (0.5 in.) aft of the leading edge of each fin' (p.4). This closes the open question in scorecard-finsoff-2026-08-25.md section 5 item 3: the fully-turbulent friction assumption is the RIGHT one for this cell and cannot be blamed for our excess. Also: Re held at 9.8e6 per metre (3.0e6 per foot) through the Mach range; stagnation temperature 322 K; 1/2-scale models; 2.54-cm (1-in.) sting extending 29.21 cm aft of the base to a 19.2-deg half-angle flare; S is the maximum cross-sectional area of the body, the same reference our kernel uses.

THE BASE PANEL (C_A,b) IS DIGITIZED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT GATED. Convention established from the report and DEMONSTRATED, not guessed: C_A,b = base axial force / qS = -C_p,b x (A_b/S), i.e. the same sign convention as our kernel's powerOff.base, with C_A,corr = C_A - C_A,b. Demonstration on known points: Figures 3 (short) and 5 (long) plot C_p,b against alpha, and -C_p,b x 0.4225 reproduces both branches of the Fig 11/12 base panel to <= 0.004 - e.g. short model M0.91, predicted fins-on -0.0135 and fins-off -0.0304 against read -0.0128 and -0.0300; short M0.60 fins-off predicted -0.0275 against read -0.0293. That cross-check also fixes which branch is which, which the line styles alone cannot. IT IS NOT GATED because the measured base is a sting artefact rather than a free base: C_p,b is POSITIVE (base pressure ABOVE free stream) at alpha = 0 over M0.60-0.90, so the measured base axial force is a THRUST of 0.02-0.04 in CD, which our kernel cannot produce at any Mach and should not be asked to. The report says the same thing (p.5): 'The base axial-force coefficients were generally negative at Mach numbers less than 1.00 and were positive at a Mach number of 1.20. This trend is characteristic of boattailed afterbodies and is also associated with sting diameter and flare angle.' Digitized fins-off C_A,b for the record, short model: -0.029 (M0.60), -0.033 (0.65), -0.036 (0.70), -0.041 (0.75), -0.033 (0.90), -0.018 (0.95), -0.021 (1.00), -0.015 (1.10), +0.023 (1.15), +0.026 (1.20); long model: -0.024 (0.60), -0.024 (0.65), -0.026 (0.70), -0.031 (0.75), -0.039 (0.90), -0.037 (0.95), -0.022 (1.00), -0.028 (1.05), -0.031 (1.10), -0.036 (1.15), -0.042 (1.20). Read accuracy ~+/-0.005. Gating them would need a cdBase quantity in score.mjs; do not add one until there is a base measurement with no sting in it.

THERE IS NO FINS-OFF x_cp CURVE TO GATE. The Fig 11/12 legend lists 'Fins off' for the whole figure, but the x_cp panel draws only the delta_F = 0 and delta_F = 2 curves - checked blob by blob across both panels and both scans, never more than two curves at any Mach. A finless ARCAS body's CP sits around 40-50 %L, off the bottom of a panel that spans 70-90 %L.

maxMach is 1.3: TN D-4013 stops at M1.20 and there is no fins-off measurement above it anywhere in the anchor set - the fact that made the six ARCAS supersonic gates un-attributable to the fin term in scorecard-junction-2026-08-25.md.

THIS CELL IS THE CLEAN ONE OF THE PAIR. p.3 of the report: on the LONG model the fin slots were 'plugged with balsa and faired flush with the model skin' for the fins-off runs, where on the SHORT model the un-faired fin anchors were left in as the plugs. So the long fins-off article carries no protuberance our fixture fails to model, and the short one does. Where the two cells disagree about our body error, this one is the better-posed comparison.

GATED AT THE REPORT'S OWN TEST MACH NUMBERS ONLY - 0.60, 0.80, 0.90, 1.00, 1.20. The long model was NOT run at M0.95 ('The short model was also investigated at a Mach number of 0.95', p.4), so this cell gates five points to the short cell's six and its M0.95 read sits in the fairing series.

THE PAIR IS STILL THE HARNESS'S ONLY MEASURED CHECK ON HOW OUR SKIN FRICTION SCALES WITH BODY LENGTH: the two configs differ by 12.55 in of cylinder and - on the fins-off runs only - by the plug treatment, the short model's slots carrying its un-faired fin anchors where the long model's were faired flush. On the report-scan reads the tunnel's own increment at M0.60 is 0.2491 - 0.2214 = 0.0277, and it is an UNDERSTATEMENT of the clean-body increment, because the anchor drag sits in the SUBTRAHEND: long_clean - (short_clean + anchors) = clean_increment - anchors, so the clean increment is 0.0277 + anchors. What the anchors make an UPPER bound is the RATIO of our increment to the tunnel's - 0.0512 / 0.0277 = 1.85x at M0.60, i.e. our friction over-scales on added length by AT MOST 1.85x, and that bound is not tight because the anchor drag has never been quantified. CORRECTED 2026-09-21: this read 'OVERSTATEMENT' from 2026-08-25, having attached the section 5.2 bound to the increment instead of to the ratio.

Note the report itself remarks that 'the base axial-force coefficient is negative for the fins-off configuration at a Mach number of 1.20' for the long model (p.5), which the read reproduces (-0.042), where the short model's goes positive - the report attributes that difference to the short model's fin anchors.

basic-finner-fig23._provenance: Karbon, 'Assessing the Accuracy of Aerodynamics Simulation Through CFD and Flight Testing' (NAR Research and Development report, vNARCON, 21 February 2026; local copy docs/User files/Buckeye Files/Accessing_the_Accuracy_of_Aerodynamic_Simulation_KKarbon.pdf), appendix Figure 23, PDF p38: Army-Navy Basic Finner Cx0 against Mach, series 'DRDC WT' (grey circles). Karbon cites Bhagwandin & Sahu, ARL 2013 (DTIC ADA592550) for the figure; the DRDC wind-tunnel source report behind the legend is NOT yet chased (open-items section 3, Harness coverage), so this is a reproduction of a reproduction and stays INFORMATIONAL. It is the only Finner drag data in the harness below M1.05 (the gated DREV-TM-9703 Table VIII free-flight series starts at M1.056; the subsonic ANF set was never retrieved). Read 2026-10-11 off the figure's embedded 1259x747 raster: axes calibrated from the gridlines (M 0.50 at x=127.5 px, 245 px per Mach; Cx0 0.20 at y=660.5 px, 37.94 px per 0.05), unoccluded markers located by template match and connected-component centroid (the two agree within 0.003 in Cx0 and 0.01 in Mach), occluded markers (M0.93, M1.05, M1.35) placed by eye on a 4x ruled enlargement. Calibration check: the same procedure on the figure's 'DRDC FF MF' series gives (1.052, 0.867), (2.371, 0.482), (3.731, 0.305) against Table VIII's tabulated (1.056, 0.868), (2.364, 0.478), (3.745, 0.309) - within 0.005, and within about 0.01 elsewhere where the figure appears to plot a fitted mean of several shots. Tolerance: +/-0.010 (that calibration agreement; the source states no accuracy), +/-0.015 on the three occluded markers (third element). Scored at alpha 0 (Cx0 is the zero-yaw axial coefficient; the gated free-flight cell scores at 2 deg to match its yaw fits) and at ISA sea level: the tunnel Reynolds number is not given, so a friction bias of unknown sign remains, worst subsonic.

series.source: Karbon NAR R&D report (vNARCON 2026) Fig 23 (PDF p38), 'DRDC WT' series, reproduced from Bhagwandin & Sahu ARL 2013; figure read +/-0.010 (+/-0.015 occluded); DRDC source not yet chased; informational, never counted.

r100-78-finned._provenance: NASA TR R-100 (Stoney 1961), https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19630004995 , config 78 data sheet PDF p95 (Figure 10 systematic series): C_D,T against Mach, helium-gun free flight, no sting. A PLAIN-BODY (no boat-tail) cell: parabolic nose straight into a cylinder, with the report's three thin type-A fins on. Values: docs/research/Boat-tails/fig10-digitised/manual-read1.json (Claude, 2026-10-08: one careful manual read of the deskewed, gridline-calibrated sheet, +/-0.003, +/-0.01 on the steep M0.975-1.00 points; an automatic tracer agreed within 0.008 wherever it followed the right line). Per-point tolerance (third element) = quadrature sum of the report's own stated accuracy (p6: Delta C_D = +/-0.01 and Delta M = +/-0.01, from repeat flights of identical models), the reading resolution, and the stated Mach error times the read curve's local slope. INFORMATIONAL (gate false): a single reader, not two independent reads, and the fins' drag is inside the measured total - promote only after a second independent read.

series.source: NASA TR R-100 config 78 sheet (PDF p95): measured total C_D,T, three type-A fins on; single manual read; per-point tol = hypot(0.01 stated, reading, 0.01 x slope); informational, never counted.

A BOAT-TAILED-BODY cell: the identical nose and three fins cancel in the measured difference (the report found fin interference small on these thin fins), so the increment is what the boattail itself does to total drag. Values: manual-read1.json (single manual read; see the r100-*-finned cells). Per-point tolerance (third element) = quadrature of the stated +/-0.01 for each of the two configurations, both reading resolutions, and both configurations' stated Mach error (+/-0.01) times the local slope of each read curve. INFORMATIONAL (gate false): single reader, and fin-afterbody interference is assumed to cancel. Kernel side: cdDelta = total CD of this finless fixture minus total CD of r100-98.json, same flags and conditions (sea-level ISA reproduces the sheets' Re).

r100-23._provenance: NASA TR R-100 (Stoney 1961), https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19630004995 , config 23 data sheet PDF p40: C_D,T against Mach, helium-gun free flight, no sting. THE SMALL-MODEL CELL: a 1.00 in body with three fins of 12.4 x its cross-section in exposed planform - the oversized-fin regime goblin-29.CDX1 raised (open-items section 3, Harness coverage) - measured over M0.85-1.25 (the sheet has no data below M0.85, so the subsonic M0.3 end of that question stays unanchored). Values: one read (Claude, 2026-10-11) of the 300-dpi page render, per-column trace calibrated from the gridlines with a local correction for the 0.26 deg scan skew, checked by eye; reading resolution +/-0.003 (from M1.18 the curve lies on the 0.50 gridline). Per-point tolerance (third element) = quadrature of the report's stated accuracy (p6: Delta C_D +/-0.01, Delta M +/-0.01), the reading resolution, and the stated Mach error times the read curve's local slope. INFORMATIONAL (gate false): a single reader, and two geometry approximations (the curved nose section as a power-0.5 transition; fins on the cylinder overhanging the boattail) - see the fixture _notes.

series.source: NASA TR R-100 config 23 sheet (PDF p40): measured total C_D,T, fins on; single read; per-point tol = hypot(0.01 stated, 0.003 reading, 0.01 x slope); informational, never counted.
